description: Fresh modern Hebrew prose from eight catalogue authors absent from the original four-author pilot, with 24 reference works, four calibration-only unfamiliar-author works and four final unfamiliar-author works.
selection_protocol: Before any scoring, propose authors based on primary catalogue availability of original Hebrew prose. Select six independent complete modern narratives per reference author and two per unfamiliar author. Require 2000 to 30000 normalized tokens after unchanged extraction. Exclude metadata with translators or foreign original language, obvious biblical/historical retellings, folklore collections, multi-volume/chapter fragments, duplicates and ambiguous editorial-preface layouts. Inspect headings and body openings/endings for independent narrative and leakage. For Yehuda Steinberg inspect the first 60 prose records and exclude ambiguous [part/version] titles and allegorical voyages; for Asher Barash skip early historical tales and long novels, then take six eligible modern short narratives; for other authors inspect first 20 eligible catalogue entries and select modern prose consistent with the shared broad genre. No classifier outcomes, features, thresholds or accuracy were consulted.
role_assignment_basis: Root approved the proposed four-reference/two-calibration/two-final unfamiliar split before scoring. During source-only audit the proposed final unfamiliar Jacob Steinberg was replaced by Alexander Ziskind Rabinovich because the former writer's Hebrew/Yiddish self-translation history complicated the original-language criterion. Other author roles were unchanged. This was an attribution-language curation decision, not an observed performance response.

freshness.curator_actions: Catalogue/rights/author metadata review, complete source downloads, inspection of headings/openings/endings, existing extraction, token counts, source/text checksums and exact duplicate/old-author-overlap checks only. No classification, feature analysis, fitted models, predictions or benchmark execution.
freshness.caveat: David Frischman candidates had been read during initial corpus feasibility research, but were never selected in the original benchmark or scored; all new authors remain unexposed to classification-performance evaluation at acquisition. Subsequent test exposure must be tracked by the evaluator.

attribution_caveat: Four reference authors, two calibration unfamiliar authors and two final unfamiliar authors form a small convenience sample. The total of eight labels is not eight candidate authors or eight independent unfamiliar-author trials. Original-Hebrew status follows the primary catalogue and limited source review; historical self-translation cannot be excluded globally. Genre/topic labels are broad and not an independently matched study. These modern Hebrew texts cannot validate Biblical Hebrew, Aramaic, named scripture attribution, author counts or Arabic/Greek transfer. Editorial, chronological and subject confounds remain. Final unfamiliar authors must stay out of model and threshold fitting.
parser_policy: Use unchanged benyehuda-html-v1 to remove head/title metadata, headings, explicitly marked footnotes/references, and the marked publisher footer while retaining prose outside paragraph markup. No model-dependent cleaning. Use existing Hebrew tokenizer; hbo is the implementation key, actual source language is modern Hebrew heb.
label_policy: literary_prose and modern_social_and_psychological_fiction are manual broad challenge strata; they do not prove fine-grained topic matching. Story themes, social settings, narrator styles and editorial conventions can differ among authors.
